points: The next print will reveal whether Q3 2026 revenue kept up with Q2's $149.7 million, 51.7% year-over-year pace, and management's Q4 guidance will show if that growth is durable into the holiday quarter. Strong follow-through would justify staying long because it turns one record quarter into a trend.

Q3 2026 GMV will show whether the $1.278 billion Q2 volume, up 37.9%, is still accelerating; BNPL spending typically rises into year-end, so a strong Q3 sets up a bigger Q4. That matters for the long because volume drives merchant fees and loan-book scale.

The next report will show if active subscribers held near the 854,000 level after jumping 76.4% year over year in Q2; subscriber retention is what converts one-time users into recurring revenue. Sustained growth supports the long case that Sezzle is building a sticky customer base.

Progress toward a national bank charter could lower funding costs and let Sezzle offer new products over the next 12-18 months; any update on timing or approval steps in the next print would de-risk that catalyst. That matters because cheaper funding directly improves margins.

Credit losses spiked 109% year over year in Q3 2025 and the provision is now only 2% of GMV, so the next few prints must show losses are not outpacing growth. If defaults stay controlled, profitability holds; if not, the long thesis weakens.

Total debt is $131.39 million, a heavy load versus $149.7 million in quarterly revenue, so the path of cash flow and debt reduction over the next year matters more than the current growth rate. Deleveraging in coming quarters would reduce refinancing risk and support the long.

The Connecticut and North Carolina attorney-general inquiries create headline risk; the next 12-18 months will show whether fines stay small or expand. As long as regulatory costs stay below the $10 million falsifier threshold, the growth story remains intact.

NDAQ reports on October 22, 2026, and its tone on fintech volumes and credit could set risk appetite for the sector before Sezzle's own print. A constructive peer read would support the active theme and make this a timely long entry.
